title: Additive total tensor commutes with cones before localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] additive in both variables. Assume countable coproducts exist and tensoring on either side with any object preserves them. Use integer cochain complexes, the cone $C(u)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ of $u:X\to Y$ with differential $\begin{pmatrix}d_Y&u\\0&-d_X\end{pmatrix}$, the derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ and its localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For every complex $P$ and cochain map $u:X\to Y$, there is an isomorphism in the derived category
$$Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes C(u))\cong Q C(1_P\otimes u).$$
It is induced by a chain isomorphism $\phi_{P,u}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes C(u))\cong C(1_P\otimes u)$ natural in $P$ and in commutative squares between arrows $u$, and satisfying $\phi_{P,u}\circ(1_P\otimes i_u)=i_{1_P\otimes u}$, where $i_u:Y\to C(u)$ is the cone inclusion. No acyclicity, boundedness, flatness, closedness, enough-projectives, or exactness-of-countable-coproducts hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Specialize the proved CochainComplex.mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso P u (curriedTensor C) to obtain the entire family of chain isomorphisms. Mathlib tensorObj and tensorHom are abbreviations for mapBifunctor and mapBifunctorMap for this bifunctor. Countable coproducts supply HasMapBifunctor for all integer cochain complexes; MonoidalPreadditive supplies additivity. The upstream construction already performs the signed summand construction and differential check of the original steps 1-3, so no new coproduct calculation is needed here.

Apply the proved mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso_hom_naturality with F = curriedTensor C to obtain simultaneous naturality in the first complex and a commutative arrow square. Its square proof is exactly mapBifunctorMap_comm in the statement. Apply mapBifunctorMap_inr_mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso_hom to obtain compatibility with the cone inclusion. Both assertions have definitionally the required tensorObj/tensorHom types.

For each P and u take e to be DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso of the chain isomorphism chosen in step 1. Its hom is definitionally Q.map of the chosen hom, so the required equality is reflexivity. This only applies a functor to an isomorphism and does not require descent of the tensor functor, flatness or boundedness.

Source: I read Stacks derived.tex Tag 0G6E (remark-double-complex-as-tensor-product-of, lines 3535-3590), which proves only that Tot is exact on K, so the explicit cone calculation is correctly recorded as an agent proof. Step 1: lem-sfb-left-resolution-additive-finite-coproducts (Mathlib leaf preservesFiniteCoproductsOfAdditive, line 213) applies to P^p⊗− because the tensor is additive in each variable; the regrouping of the integer-indexed sums into B^n⊕A^{n+1} is correct and uses only countable coproducts. Steps 2-3: I recomputed the signs. The source differential on P^p⊗X^{q+1} gives coefficients ε_p, ε_{p+1}, −1 after φ; φ followed by the cone matrix of t gives ε_p, −ε_p, −1, and ε_{p+1}=−ε_p, so they agree. The Y family agrees as well, so φ is a chain isomorphism. Step 4: the cone map diag(b,a[1]) is a chain map because u'a=bu; both sides give f^p⊗b^q on the Y family and ε_p f^p⊗a^{q+1} on the X family, which proves naturality in P and in arrow squares simultaneously. Step 5: φ(1⊗i_u)=i_t on the Y family, and Q applied to the chain isomorphism gives the derived isomorphism without claiming that T(P,−) descends to D. Each cited statement says what its step takes from it. Edge cases checked: P=0, u=id, P in odd degree (the sign is needed), characteristic 2, unbounded complexes. The hypothesis that tensoring preserves countable coproducts is never used, which is harmless. lean.statement: theorem exists_totalTensorConeComparison (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [MonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalPreadditive C] [HasCountableCoproducts C] [TensorPreservesCountableCoproducts C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] : ∃ φ : ∀ (P X Y : CochainComplex C ℤ) (u : X ⟶ Y), HomologicalComplex.tensorObj P (mappingCone u) ≅ mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P) u), (∀ (P P' X Y X' Y' : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : P ⟶ P') (u : X ⟶ Y) (u' : X' ⟶ Y') (a : X ⟶ X') (b : Y ⟶ Y') (h : u ≫ b = a ≫ u'), HomologicalComplex.tensorHom f (mappingCone.map u u' a b h) ≫ (φ P' X' Y' u').hom = (φ P X Y u).hom ≫ mappingCone.map (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P) u) (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P') u') (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom f a) (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom f b) (mapBifunctorMap_comm (curriedTensor C) f u u' a b h)) ∧ (∀ (P X Y : CochainComplex C ℤ) (u : X ⟶ Y), HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P) (mappingCone.inr u) ≫ (φ P X Y u).hom = mappingCone.inr (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P) u)) ∧ (∀ (P X Y : CochainComplex C ℤ) (u : X ⟶ Y), ∃ e : (DerivedCategory.Q (C := C)).obj (HomologicalComplex.tensorObj P (mappingCone u)) ≅ (DerivedCategory.Q (C := C)).obj (mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (𝟙 P) u)), e.hom = (DerivedCategory.Q (C := C)).map (φ P X Y u).hom)
